title: Jonah and the Drop
premise: Kestrel Crane, a veteran air-crash investigator, has spent twelve years quietly probing the downing of Flight 4471, which killed her husband and daughter in row twelve. A routine voiceprint match unlocks a shadow server in Reykjavik containing proof that the crash was engineered to silence a whistleblower inside a defense contractor protected by three governments. As Kestrel smuggles the evidence across borders pursued by an assassin who once saved her life, she discovers her own testimony was falsified years ago and that the leak's source is someone she trusted. In the end she trades her anonymity for exposure, broadcasting the truth at the cost of her career and nearly her life, and finally buries the past by telling it whole.
about_author: Astrid Halloran is a former aviation safety analyst who left the industry after a decade of reports she says were 'filed into silence.' She writes thrillers from a coastal town in Norway, where the fog does most of the foreshadowing.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Twelve years after Flight 4471, Kestrel works crash sites with surgical detachment until a voiceprint analysis flags a voice she archived long ago. The emotional beat is grief held at arm's length beginning to crack.

chapters.title: The Reykjavik Key
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Following the voiceprint to Iceland, she uses her credentials to open a hidden server and finds flight data proving 4471 was brought down deliberately. Fear replaces grief as she realizes what she now carries.

chapters.title: Rules That Rewrite Themselves
chapters.summary: Alternating POV with her old mentor, Director Osei, who orders the investigation closed and her credentials revoked. Kestrel sees the machinery of cover-up close around her; the beat is betrayal by institutions she served.

chapters.title: The Man Who Saved Her
chapters.summary: Assassin Marek Voss's POV. He is assigned to erase the leak and recognizes Kestrel from a rescue years ago. Duty and debt collide; the emotional beat is a killer discovering he has a conscience.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Truth
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She contacts a journalist in Berlin and learns every official channel is compromised across three countries. Paranoia sharpens into resolve: the truth must go public or die with her.

chapters.title: What She Signed
chapters.summary: Flashback-heavy chapter, Kestrel's POV. She uncovers that her own post-crash testimony was doctored under her signature, making her complicit for twelve years. Shame becomes fuel.

chapters.title: The Whistleblower's Face
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The server's source is revealed: Osei himself, dying and guilt-ridden, who has been feeding Kestrel breadcrumbs. Loyalty and truth tear in opposite directions as Voss closes in.

chapters.title: Cold Harbor
chapters.summary: Voss's POV. Ordered to finish the job, he corners Kestrel in a Norwegian harbor town but lets her go, burning his own handler instead. The beat is his final choice of debt over duty.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, climax. With Osei dead and agencies hunting her, she hijacks a safety-conference feed to release everything—data, names, her own falsified report. Voss shields her escape at terrible cost.

chapters.title: Telling It Whole
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, resolution. Months later, disgraced but cleared, she testifies publicly and visits row twelve's memorial for the first time without flinching. Grief integrates into purpose; invisibility ends on her own terms.
